Implementing Acts
Implementing Acts refer to specific actions taken to execute the provisions outlined in a legal framework, which may include various procedural guidelines.<SEP>Implementing acts are specific rules adopted by the European Commission to ensure uniform application of EU legislation.

Examination Procedure
Examination Procedure represents a systematic method for evaluating and approving implementing acts, ensuring compliance with legislative standards.

data.entity_name: Regulation of the European Parliament and the Council
data.content:
Regulation of the European Parliament and the Council
A regulation that outlines essential cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements and high-risk AI systems.

ENISA
ENISA is the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity responsible for providing cybersecurity solutions and frameworks for member states and organizations within the EU.<SEP>ENISA, the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, is responsible for enhancing the cybersecurity framework within the EU and assists in issues related to AI systems.<SEP>ENISA, the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, is a permanent member of the advisory forum, providing insights on cybersecurity issues.<SEP>ENISA is the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity that provides expertise and advice on cybersecurity aspects pertaining to the Regulation.

Regulation (EU) 2019/881
Regulation (EU) 2019/881 is a legislative act of the European Parliament and Council that outlines ENISA's tasks and cooperation on cybersecurity matters.<SEP>Regulation (EU) 2019/881 specifically focuses on cybersecurity measures and tasks for ENISA regarding the certification of digital products.<SEP>Regulation (EU) 2019/881 is a legislative measure concerning the governance of high-risk AI systems, focusing on data governance and cybersecurity requirements.<SEP>Regulation (EU) 2019/881 refers to the European Union regulation pertaining to cybersecurity for AI systems, including compliance and certification processes.

Horizontal Cybersecurity Requirements
A set of cybersecurity requirements that apply to various products with digital elements across the European Union.

Critical Products with Digital Elements
Products that are deemed essential and require a high level of cybersecurity assurance under EU regulations.

Conformity Assessment Procedure
The Conformity Assessment Procedure is a structured evaluation process defined in Annex VI, aimed at determining whether AI systems comply with established safety and rights standards. This procedure is crucial for ensuring that products, particularly high-risk AI systems, meet necessary regulatory and cybersecurity requirements before they are developed, deployed, and marketed. It encompasses a series of evaluations that providers must follow, which ensures that these systems adhere to legal standards and effectively protect users' rights and safety. Overall, the Conformity Assessment Procedure plays a vital role in validating that AI systems align with regulations designed to safeguard public interests.<SEP>The Conformity Assessment Procedure is a systematic process required for evaluating compliance of high-risk AI systems with established regulations and safety standards.

Regulation (EU) No 526/2013
Regulation (EU) No 526/2013, known as the Cybersecurity Act, is the previous framework governing ENISA's operations before its revision under Regulation (EU) 2019/881.

Cybersecurity Act
The Cybersecurity Act refers to Regulation (EU) No 526/2013 which was repealed and replaced by Regulation (EU) 2019/881, influencing the legal framework for cybersecurity in the EU.

Cybersecurity of AI Systems
Cybersecurity of AI Systems refers to protecting artificial intelligence technologies from cyber threats and ensuring security standards are met.

AI Innovation
AI Innovation refers to the development and application of new artificial intelligence technologies aimed at improving various sectors and ensuring compliance with legal frameworks.

Legal Framework
A Legal Framework is a structured set of laws and regulations that govern the operation of technologies, particularly in ensuring ethical and safe development.<SEP>Legal Framework encompasses the set of regulations and standards that govern the development and implementation of AI systems, ensuring they meet compliance and ethical considerations.

Evidence-Based Regulatory Learning
Evidence-Based Regulatory Learning is the process by which authorities gather insights from regulatory sandboxes to improve and adapt legal frameworks based on actual data and outcomes.

Emerging Risks
Emerging Risks refer to new potential dangers that arise from the development and deployment of AI technologies, which regulatory bodies aim to understand and mitigate.

National or European Standardisation Organisations
National or European Standardisation Organisations are entities that set technical standards for AI systems to ensure quality and interoperability within regulatory frameworks.

Stakeholder and Civil Society Organisations
Stakeholder and civil society organisations involve various groups that engage in discussing and influencing AI policies and regulations.

Standardisation Organisations
Standardisation Organisations are groups that develop and promote standards to ensure the quality and safety of products and services, including AI technologies.

AI Applications
AI applications refer to various innovative technologies and software solutions that utilize artificial intelligence for different purposes.

Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012
Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 establishes a comprehensive framework for standardization procedures within the European Union, aiming to enhance both the consistency and quality of standards across member states. This regulation significantly influences the assessment of compliance for AI systems, as well as the broader landscape of national measures related to standardization. By promoting harmonized standards, Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 fosters competitiveness and growth in the single market. It outlines the specific needs for clear and consistent standards, thus impacting the development and conformity processes not only for various industries but particularly for artificial intelligence systems within the EU.<SEP>Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 outlines the procedures for standardisation and the role of the European Commission in assessing harmonised standards.<SEP>Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 pertains to the European standardization policy, outlining procedures for the preparation and adoption of technical standards to facilitate trade.<SEP>Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 pertains to the governance of standardization processes within the European Union.

AI Practices
AI Practices encompass guidelines and prohibitions established to ensure the ethical and safe deployment of artificial intelligence technologies.<SEP>AI Practices encompass the set of regulations and ethical standards that must be followed for AI systems within the EU.<SEP>AI practices refer to the specific uses and methodologies of artificial intelligence systems that must comply with the regulations filed under the European Data Protection Regulation.

Article 79(5)
Article 79(5) outlines the notification requirements and timelines for responses by market surveillance authorities regarding AI regulations.

Articles 40 and 41
Articles 40 and 41 refer to specific sections within the EU regulation that detail harmonised standards and common specifications.<SEP>Articles 40 and 41 specify harmonised standards and common specifications which are critical for assessing AI compliance and practices.

National Measure
A National Measure refers to any regulatory decision or action taken by a Member State that must comply with European Union regulations.

Shortcomings in AI System
Shortcomings in AI Systems refer to deficiencies that may lead to non-compliance with regulations, impacting their acceptance by the Commission.

AI Technologies
AI Technologies encompass a variety of tools and systems designed to enhance processes across various industries by leveraging data, algorithms, and automation.<SEP>AI Technologies refer to the suite of advanced systems and methods developed within the field of Artificial Intelligence, which require oversight for responsible innovation.<SEP>AI Technologies refer to the range of technologies related to artificial intelligence that national authorities must understand and regulate.<SEP>AI technologies encompass various advancements in artificial intelligence that require regular oversight and regulation for safety and compliance.

Regulatory Oversight
Regulatory Oversight is the process of monitoring and controlling the development and deployment of technologies, ensuring they comply with legal frameworks and safety standards.

Innovative AI Systems
Innovative AI Systems are newly developed applications of artificial intelligence that necessitate rigorous testing and evaluation before market introduction.

Regulatory Sandbox
A Regulatory Sandbox is a controlled environment where new technologies, such as AI systems, can be tested under regulatory supervision to ensure safety and compliance.

Transitional Period
The Transitional Period is a phase during which compliance with the new Regulation is being encouraged among providers of high-risk AI systems.

Regulation for High-Risk AI Systems
Regulation for High-Risk AI Systems is the set of guidelines and obligations designed to govern the use and development of AI technologies that present significant risks to society.

Directive (EU) 2022/2557
Directive (EU) 2022/2557 focuses on the resilience of critical entities and replaces the previous directive from 2008, emphasizing enhancements in critical infrastructure.<SEP>Directive (EU) 2022/2557 is a legal framework within the European Union that addresses the management of critical digital infrastructure.<SEP>Directive (EU) 2022/2557 is a legislative act concerning the resilience of critical infrastructure to threats and emergencies.<SEP>The Directive (EU) 2022/2557 focuses on the resilience of critical entities and pertains to law enforcement and safety regulations.<SEP>Directive (EU) 2022/2557 relates to the establishment of laws regarding the protection of individuals' rights in the context of AI and technology.

Critical Infrastructure
Critical Infrastructure refers to essential systems and assets that are crucial for the functioning of society and the economy. This includes vital services such as energy, transportation, communication, road traffic, water supply, gas, heating, and electricity. The disruption of these critical services can threaten public safety, harm health, damage property, and endanger the environment. Given the importance of these systems, there is a need for special consideration in the registration of high-risk AI systems, highlighting their significance within the framework of public safety and economic security. This definition aligns with various legal frameworks, including those outlined in EU law, which emphasize the necessity of protecting these essential systems from disruption to ensure the continued well-being of the community.

Safety Components
Safety Components are essential elements that play a critical role in ensuring the reliable and safe operation of products, particularly in the fields of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics. They are designed to protect the physical integrity of critical infrastructure and to promote the health and safety of individuals. Safety Components encompass crucial systems that not only enhance operational safety but also ensure compliance with relevant regulations governing AI systems. These components are integral to the functionality of AI systems, contributing to their safety and adherence to safety requirements as stipulated by regulatory frameworks. Overall, Safety Components are vital for safeguarding the overall safety of various products across diverse applications.

Cloud Computing Centres
Cloud computing centres are facilities housing the critical digital infrastructure systems for various applications, including cybersecurity and monitoring.

Critical Digital Infrastructure
Critical Digital Infrastructure refers to the technology systems and assets that support critical functions such as road traffic, water supply, and energy management.

Water Supply
Water Supply is a critical component of infrastructure that provides water for residential, commercial, and industrial use, which is vital for public health and safety.

Gas Supply
Gas Supply serves as a crucial infrastructure for energy needs in households and industries, influencing both safety and economic activities.

Heating Supply
Heating Supply refers to the systems in place to provide heating for buildings, which is essential for maintaining comfort and safety during colder months.

Electricity Supply
Electricity Supply is fundamental infrastructure that provides power for residential and commercial operations, making it vital for everyday functions.

Fire Alarm Systems
Fire Alarm Systems are safety components designed to detect and alert about fires, crucial for protecting lives and property.

Risk Assessment Criteria
Risk assessment criteria consist of the conditions and factors considered when evaluating the potential dangers posed by AI systems.

The European Commission
The European Commission is the executive body of the EU responsible for proposing legislation and enforcing laws, including those pertaining to AI systems and their risks.

Reports
Reports are documents that provide evidence or findings related to the performance or impact of AI systems, often submitted to authorities to highlight concerns or violations.

AI Deployment
AI Deployment refers to the implementation and application of artificial intelligence systems in various sectors, which raises legal and ethical considerations.

Reported Allegations
Reported Allegations are claims presented to authorities regarding potential harm or wrongful actions related to AI systems.

Political Opinions
Political opinions refer to individuals' beliefs and positions regarding political issues, which may be inferred from biometric data.

Trade Union Membership
Trade union membership indicates an individual's affiliation to a labor union, which can be deduced from biometric data in some instances.

Religious Beliefs
Religious beliefs encompass an individual's spiritual and philosophical convictions, which may be inferred through biometric data analysis.

Philosophical Beliefs
Philosophical beliefs reflect an individual's personal worldview or ideology, which might be ascertained from analysis of biometric data.

Sex Life
Sex life pertains to an individual's sexual practices and orientations, potentially inferred through biometric categorisation systems.

Sexual Orientation
Sexual orientation is mentioned as a demographic factor that could lead to discrimination influenced by AI systems in recruitment and employment evaluations.<SEP>Sexual orientation refers to individuals' patterns of emotional, romantic or sexual attraction, which might also be deduced through biometric data.

Union harmonisation legislation
Union harmonisation legislation encompasses laws that ensure products meet consistent standards across Member States.<SEP>Union harmonisation legislation refers to a set of regulatory requirements designed to ensure products meet safety and performance standards across member states.<SEP>Union harmonisation legislation refers to a set of legal standards within the European Union that ensure the uniformity of technical regulations for products, including high-risk AI systems.<SEP>Union harmonisation legislation sets the regulatory framework within which high-risk AI systems must comply, particularly when related to product safety.

Article 9
Article 9 refers to a specific section of regulatory legislation that outlines risk management systems applicable to AI systems.

Section A of Annex I
Section A of Annex I contains a list of Union harmonisation legislation that applies to products containing AI systems, defining compliance requirements.<SEP>Section A of Annex I outlines specific products and requirements related to Union harmonisation legislation that pertain to AI systems.

AI-related technologies
AI-related technologies encompass various tools and systems that utilize artificial intelligence and must adhere to defined regulations.

Annex XIII
Annex XIII outlines specific criteria and benchmarks to assess the impact capabilities of AI models.<SEP>Annex XIII provides the criteria for assessing whether a general-purpose AI model presents systemic risks and is subject to updates by The Commission.<SEP>Annex XIII specifies the criteria for determining which general-purpose AI models present systemic risks and may be updated by the Commission.

High Impact Capabilities
High impact capabilities refer to the potential effects that a general-purpose AI model can have, evaluated using specific technical tools and methodologies.

Thresholds
Thresholds are the predefined limits set by the Commission to classify AI models based on their training computations and capabilities.

High-Risk Use Cases
High-Risk Use Cases refer to specific situations or deployments of AI systems that are deemed high-risk according to the regulations set by the EU.

Cybersecurity Risks
Cybersecurity Risks refer to potential threats and vulnerabilities associated with data breaches and misuse of technology, relevant in the context of managing the EU database.

Functional Specifications
Functional Specifications involve defining the required features and functions of the EU database to ensure it meets the regulatory needs.

Asylum and Border Control Management
Asylum and Border Control Management includes systems for processing asylum requests and overseeing border security, highlighting areas where high-risk AI systems are applicable.

Article 24 of the Charter
Article 24 specifically addresses the rights of children, ensuring their protection and welfare.

United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child
The UN Convention focuses on the rights and protection of children worldwide, emphasizing their vulnerabilities.

UNCRC General Comment No 25
UNCRC General Comment No 25 relates to the digital environment, providing guidance on children's rights in that context.

Human Dignity
Human Dignity is a fundamental principle recognizing the inherent value of every individual, forming the basis for various rights.<SEP>Human dignity is a fundamental ethical consideration ensuring respect for individuals in the context of AI and technology.

data.content:
Respect for Private and Family Life
Respect for Private and Family Life is a fundamental right that protects individuals' personal and familial privacy from interference.

Protection of Personal Data
Protection of Personal Data is a fundamental right that safeguards personal information from misuse and unauthorized access.

Freedom of Expression and Information
Freedom of Expression and Information allows individuals to express themselves and obtain information freely.

Freedom of Assembly and Association
Freedom of Assembly and Association grants individuals the right to gather and collectively voice their opinions or interests.

Right to Non-Discrimination
The Right to Non-Discrimination ensures that individuals are treated equally without bias based on race, gender, or other characteristics.

Right to Education
The Right to Education guarantees access to education for all individuals, recognizing its importance for personal and societal development.

Consumer Protection
Consumer Protection rights are designed to safeguard buyers against unfair practices in the marketplace.

Workers Rights
Workers' Rights refer to the rights that protect individuals in their workplace, including fair treatment, safe conditions, and fair compensation.

Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Rights of Persons with Disabilities ensure that individuals with disabilities have equitable access to opportunities and accommodations.

Gender Equality
Gender Equality refers to the state of equal access to resources and opportunities irrespective of gender.<SEP>Gender Equality refers to the state of equal access to resources and opportunities regardless of gender, addressing social, economic, and political disparities.

Right to an Effective Remedy
The Right to an Effective Remedy ensures that individuals have access to justice and avenues for redress when their rights are violated.

Right to a Fair Trial
The Right to a Fair Trial guarantees that individuals receive impartial legal proceedings.

Right of Defence
The Right of Defence ensures that individuals have the opportunity to contest accusations against them.

Presumption of Innocence
The Presumption of Innocence is a legal principle that ensures individuals are considered innocent until proven guilty.

Right to Good Administration
The Right to Good Administration ensures that individuals receive fair and competent administrative treatment.

Rights of Children
The Rights of Children refer to specific protections and entitlements granted to minors to safeguard their well-being and development.

Childrens Vulnerabilities
Children’s Vulnerabilities highlight the particular risks and challenges faced by minors that require specialized attention and protection.

Level of Environmental Protection
The Level of Environmental Protection is the standard ensuring that environmental rights and health are safeguarded.

Health and Safety of Persons
Health and Safety of Persons refers to the rights ensuring the physical well-being and safety of individuals.

Directive 2014/31/EU
Directive 2014/31/EU pertains to the harmonization of the laws regarding non-automatic weighing instruments within the EU.

Directive 2014/32/EU
Directive 2014/32/EU is a legislative act by the European Parliament aimed at harmonizing laws related to measuring instruments across EU member states.<SEP>Directive 2014/32/EU relates to the harmonization of laws regarding measuring instruments made available on the market within the EU.

Relevant Organisations
Relevant organisations refer to various stakeholders involved in the development, oversight, and implementation of guidelines for high-risk AI systems.

Measurement Methodologies
Measurement methodologies are the specific methods and standards used to evaluate the performance and accuracy of AI systems.

Benchmarks
Benchmarks are standards or points of reference against which the performance of AI systems can be measured or compared.

Non-Automatic Weighing Instruments
Non-automatic weighing instruments are a category of measuring devices regulated under EU legislation for market availability and safety standards.

Measuring Instruments
Measuring instruments refer to a broad category of devices used in various sectors, subject to EU regulations for market access.

Article 68
Article 68 pertains to the establishment of a scientific panel and the criteria for appointing independent experts.

Article 101
Article 101 details the fines for failure to provide access to information requested regarding general-purpose AI models.<SEP>Article 101 is an exception within the Regulation that is not applicable from 2 August 2025.<SEP>Article 101 outlines the penalties for supplying incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information regarding AI models.

Legal Persons
Legal persons refer to entities such as companies that can represent the provider in legal matters regarding AI models.

Structured Dialogue
The structured dialogue is initiated by the AI Office to gather information about a provider's internal testing of AI models.

Access Request
The access request is a formal request made by the AI Office to access AI models for evaluation purposes.

AI model
An AI model defined as a general-purpose model is designed to perform a variety of tasks across different domains, subject to evaluations and regulatory standards.

implementing acts
Implementing acts are legal provisions established by the Commission that outline the procedures and criteria for evaluating general-purpose AI models.

law
Law refers to the system of rules which a particular country or community recognizes as regulating the actions of its members.

internal testing
Internal testing refers to the examination processes and evaluations conducted by providers on their AI models to ensure safety and effectiveness before public access.

General-Purpose AI Systems
General-purpose AI systems are versatile AI technologies that can operate independently or as parts of more complex, high-risk AI systems.

national public authorities
National public authorities are governmental bodies responsible for maintaining public order and safety, ensuring laws and regulations are followed.<SEP>National public authorities are governmental bodies responsible for supervising the application of Union law and protecting fundamental rights within their respective countries.

fundamental rights
Fundamental rights are basic human rights and freedoms that are intended to be protected by law, including equality and data protection.<SEP>Fundamental rights are basic human rights that should be protected during processes such as development, testing, and experimentation.

National Public Authorities
National Public Authorities are bodies that receive notifications of serious incidents from market surveillance authorities and play a role in the regulatory framework.<SEP>National Public Authorities are government bodies that supervise and enforce compliance with Union laws pertaining to fundamental rights and high-risk AI systems.<SEP>National Public Authorities are government entities responsible for enforcing and supervising the application of regulations, including those relating to AI and fundamental rights.<SEP>National Public Authorities are governmental bodies within Member States responsible for enforcing regulations and cooperating with market surveillance authorities on public safety matters.

Quality Management System Documentation
Quality Management System Documentation refers to the records and procedures that organizations must maintain to ensure quality control and compliance with regulations regarding AI systems.

Europol
Europol is a European Union agency for law enforcement cooperation, facilitating collaboration among EU member states' law enforcement agencies.<SEP>Europol is the European Union's law enforcement agency that assists member states in combating serious international crime and terrorism.

International Organizations
International Organizations are entities that operate across borders, often involved in cooperation with Union Member States concerning AI regulations and law enforcement.<SEP>International organizations are entities established by treaties between countries, which may engage with the Union under cooperation agreements.

Law Enforcement Cooperation
Law Enforcement Cooperation details agreements and frameworks established for cooperation between nations concerning crime prevention and judicial processes.<SEP>Law Enforcement Cooperation involves collaborative efforts among various authorities in the Union and third countries to achieve common law and order goals.

Data Processing
Data processing refers to the handling and manipulation of data by AI systems or operators for various purposes.

Safeguards
Safeguards are measures put in place to protect fundamental rights and freedoms, ensuring compliance with regulations.

Contracting Parties
Contracting parties are entities or individuals involved in agreements or treaties related to law enforcement and judicial cooperation with the Union.

International Organisations
International Organisations collaborate on global matters of governance and regulation, including AI.<SEP>International Organisations work collaboratively with Union institutions and competent authorities on regulatory and safety matters.<SEP>International organisations are entities created by treaties between governments to facilitate cooperation in areas such as law enforcement and human rights.

Adequate Safeguards
Adequate safeguards refer to the measures and policies in place to ensure the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms within law enforcement cooperation.

Fundamental Rights and Freedoms
Fundamental rights and freedoms are basic human rights that are guaranteed to individuals, which must be protected during law enforcement activities.<SEP>Fundamental rights and freedoms refer to the basic human rights enshrined in laws and regulations that protect individuals from discrimination and ensure equal treatment.

Recipient National Authorities
Recipient national authorities are the governmental bodies in charge of implementing cooperation agreements and ensuring compliance with Union law.

Law Enforcement and Judicial Cooperation
Law enforcement and judicial cooperation encompasses the agreements and frameworks established for the effective collaboration of legal authorities across borders.

Union Economy
The Union economy refers to the collective economic activities and growth opportunities available within a specified region or community, especially in the context of free and open-source software.

Open-Source Licence
An open-source licence is a type of software license that allows users to freely access, modify, and share software and data, fostering innovation and collaboration.

Software and Data
Software and data encompass a broad range of digital resources that can be used, modified, and shared under specific licensing conditions, contributing to innovation and research.

Research and Innovation
Research and innovation refer to activities aimed at creating new knowledge and solutions that can lead to advancements in various fields, driven by available technology and data.

Market
The market refers to the economic space where goods and services are exchanged, and where innovations can foster growth opportunities for economic development.<SEP>The market refers to the economic space where goods, including AI systems, are made available for purchase or deployment, subject to regulatory standards.

public law body
A public law body is responsible for overseeing the deployment of high-risk AI systems and ensuring compliance with legal standards.

private entities providing public services
Private entities that provide public services are also responsible for implementing assessments and governance measures for high-risk AI systems.

Article 6(2)
Article 6(2) refers to a specific provision that outlines the requirements for deploying high-risk AI systems.

High-Risk AI Assessment
The High-Risk AI Assessment is a required evaluation of potential impacts on fundamental rights before AI deployment.

Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments
Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments evaluate the implications of AI systems on individuals' rights and determine compliance with legal frameworks.

Data Protection Impact Assessment
Data Protection Impact Assessment is an evaluation that focuses on how data processing activities affect individuals' privacy rights and data protection.

Whistleblowers
Whistleblowers are individuals who report illicit activity within organizations, and they are protected under regulations such as Directive (EU) 2019/1937.

Undertakings
Undertakings are businesses or enterprises that collect or process personal data and must comply with data protection laws.<SEP>Undertakings refer to businesses or organizations that are subject to the Union's regulations and economic policies.

Trustworthy AI
Trustworthy AI refers to artificial intelligence technologies developed and deployed in a manner that is ethical, transparent, and respects fundamental rights and safety.<SEP>Trustworthy AI refers to artificial intelligence that aligns with the Union's values, prioritizing safety, ethics, and reliability.<SEP>Trustworthy AI refers to the development and use of artificial intelligence that meets ethical and legal standards, ensuring safety and compliance with fundamental rights.

Innovation
Innovation refers to the process of developing new technologies or improving existing technologies, which is the primary goal of establishing AI Regulatory Sandboxes.<SEP>Innovation signifies the Union's commitment to fostering new ideas and technologies, particularly in sectors like AI and sustainable practices.

Article 114 TFEU
Article 114 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union outlines processes for establishing and implementing laws that protect the internal market.

Article 16 TFEU

The directive aims to improve working conditions in platform work, setting standards for labor rights and employer responsibilities.

Regulation on AI Systems
The Regulation on AI Systems establishes a legal framework to ensure that artificial intelligence systems adhere to standards that protect fundamental rights and public safety.

Transparency in AI Systems

Comment No 25 (2021)

Council Decision 93/465/EEC

25 July 1985

OJ L 210, 7.8.1985

Member States' Laws
Member States' Laws encompass the various national regulations and legislation that must align with EU directives.

Authorized Representative
An authorized representative is a person in the Union who has received a mandate from a provider to perform duties related to AI system regulations.

Risk
Risk refers to the combination of the probability of an occurrence of harm and the severity of that harm, relating to the potential impacts of AI systems.

Placing on the Market
Placing on the market refers to the act of making an AI system available for distribution or use in the market for the first time.<SEP>Placing on the market refers to the first making available of an AI system or general-purpose AI model for commercial distribution.

Making Available on the Market
Making available on the market encompasses the supply of AI systems for distribution, whether for payment or free of charge.<SEP>Making available on the market refers to supplying an AI system or model for distribution or use in commercial activity, whether paid or free.

Putting into Service
Putting into service describes the act of supplying an AI system for first use either directly to the deployer or for their own intended purpose.<SEP>Putting into service refers to supplying an AI system for its first use directly to the deployer or for personal use.

Reasonably Foreseeable Misuse
Reasonably foreseeable misuse refers to the unintended yet predictable ways persons might use an AI system contrary to its intended purpose.

Safety Component
Safety Components are parts of an AI system that fulfill safety functions, crucial for ensuring the system does not endanger health or safety.<SEP>Safety components are elements of an AI system that fulfill safety functions, ensuring health and safety of individuals during operation.

Recall of an AI System
Recall of an AI system involves measures taken to return, disable, or remove an AI system from use that has already been made available.

Recall of AI System
The Recall of an AI System refers to the actions taken to return or disable an AI system that has been made available to users.

Withdrawal of AI System
The Withdrawal of an AI System involves measures to prevent an AI system from being made available on the market.

Performance of AI System
Performance of an AI System describes its ability to meet the intended purpose and operational requirements specified by the provider.

Human Behaviour
Human Behaviour refers to the potential misuse of AI systems resulting from interactions that deviate from their intended purposes.

Conformity Assurance
Conformity Assurance is a critical process ensuring that an AI system meets regulatory requirements and safety standards before being deployed.

AI System Performance
AI System Performance refers to how effectively an AI system operates, influenced by the quality of training data and the implementation of governance practices.<SEP>AI System Performance refers to the capability of an AI system to meet its designed objectives and operational requirements effectively.

National Authority
A National Authority is a government body involved in setting the framework for AI system compliance and overseeing the implementation of regulations.

Conformity Requirements
Conformity Requirements constitute the standards and regulations that high-risk AI systems must adhere to in order to be deemed compliant.

Third-Party Activities
Third-Party Activities include various measures undertaken by independent bodies to ensure compliance and validation of AI systems.

Substantial Modification
Substantial Modification entails significant changes made to an AI system that could affect its compliance with established requirements.

Training Data
Training Data refers to the datasets used to teach AI systems and optimize their learning and performance.<SEP>Training data consists of the datasets that are used to train AI models, impacting their performance and compliance.

CE marking
CE marking indicates an AI system's conformity with EU requirements, ensuring compliance with applicable legislation.

post-market monitoring system
A post-market monitoring system involves activities by AI system providers to gather and analyze user experiences for necessary corrective actions.

harmonised standard
A harmonised standard is defined to ensure compliance with specific requirements as outlined in Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012.<SEP>Harmonised standards are technical specifications approved by recognized standardization organizations, providing a presumption of conformity with regulations for AI model providers.

common specification
Common specifications are technical guidelines established to meet requirements set forth under relevant regulations.

training data
Training data is used to fit the parameters of an AI system, enabling it to learn and improve performance.

validation data
Validation data is utilized to evaluate a trained AI system and tune its parameters to enhance its learning process.

validation data set
A validation data set is a designated subset of training data for testing the model's performance and preventing overfitting.

testing data
Testing data serves to independently assess an AI system's expected performance prior to market launch.

input data
Input data refers to any data provided to or gathered by an AI system used to generate outputs.

biometric data
Biometric data consists of personal data derived from processing physical or behavioral characteristics of individuals.<SEP>Biometric data includes unique physical or behavioral characteristics used for identification, such as fingerprints, facial recognition data, and iris patterns.

Biometric Identification
Biometric identification is a technological process that uses unique physical characteristics to identify individuals in public, often used for law enforcement purposes.<SEP>Biometric identification is the automated recognition of individuals by comparing their biometric data against stored data in a database.<SEP>Biometric identification refers to the automated recognition of human features for identity verification, utilizing physiological, physical, and behavioral traits.

Validation Data
Validation data refers to data used for evaluating the performance and tuning of AI systems to avoid issues such as underfitting or overfitting.

Validation Data Set
A validation data set is a separate subset of the training data, used to evaluate and refine the performance of an AI system.

Testing Data
Testing data is utilized to provide an independent evaluation of an AI system's performance before deployment or market introduction.

Input Data
Input Data refers to the data fed into high-risk AI systems that must be relevant and sufficiently representative of the intended application.<SEP>Input data includes the information that is provided to an AI system, which it processes to generate outputs.

Biometric Categorization System
A biometric categorization system sorts individuals into specific categories based on their biometric data, often linked to commercial services.

Remote Biometric Identification System
A remote biometric identification system uses biometric data for the recognition of individuals from a distance.

biometric verification
Biometric verification refers to the automated one-to-one verification of an individual's identity through the comparison of their biometric data to pre-existing data.

sensitive operational data
Sensitive operational data pertains to information that relates to the prevention or prosecution of criminal offenses, which is critical for maintaining the integrity of criminal proceedings.

post remote biometric identification system
This refers to a remote biometric identification system that does not operate in real-time.<SEP>This type refers to remote biometric systems that do not operate in real-time.

publicly accessible space
A physical location that can be accessed by an undetermined number of natural persons, regardless of access conditions.<SEP>A publicly accessible space is an area where the public has access, regardless of ownership or access conditions, allowing for undetermined numbers of individuals.

law enforcement authority
A public authority responsible for preventing and investigating criminal offenses, safeguarding public security, and executing criminal penalties.<SEP>The law enforcement authority includes any public body responsible for the prevention, investigation, and prosecution of criminal offenses, ensuring public security.

national competent authority
A national competent authority is a designated entity responsible for overseeing compliance with regulations, including those related to high-risk AI systems.<SEP>An authority designated to oversee AI systems and ensure compliance with established regulations within the Union.<SEP>The national competent authority is responsible for confirming the safety and validity of certificates related to high-risk AI systems within Member States.<SEP>The national competent authority is the designated body within each Member State responsible for upholding regulations and certifications.

serious incident
A serious incident is described as an event involving malfunctioning AI systems that could cause harm to individuals, critical infrastructure, or the environment.<SEP>An event resulting in severe consequences from an AI system malfunction leading to potential harm or death to individuals.<SEP>A serious incident refers to an event of significant concern or adverse effect related to the deployment of AI systems that must be reported to regulatory authorities.

public security
Public security encompasses measures and activities aimed at preventing threats and ensuring safety against criminal offenses and incidents.

non-personal data
Non-personal data includes any data that does not pertain to identifiable individuals, also defined under EU regulation.

public authority
Public authority refers to governmental bodies that enact laws, regulations, and conduct enforcement activities related to public security and criminal justice.

criminal penalties
Criminal penalties are punishments imposed by courts or authorities on individuals found guilty of violating laws.

threats to public security
Threats to public security involve risks or dangers that can harm individuals or the community, requiring preventive measures by authorities.

real-world testing plan
A real-world testing plan outlines the methodology and objectives for testing AI systems in practical conditions to ensure compliance and safety.

sandbox plan
A sandbox plan defines the framework and conditions under which new AI technologies can be developed and tested in a controlled environment.

Real-World Testing Plan
A real-world testing plan is a document that outlines the objectives and methodology for testing AI systems in real-life conditions to ensure compliance with regulations.<SEP>The real-world testing plan outlines the procedure and requirements for testing high-risk AI systems in actual operational environments.<SEP>The real-world testing plan outlines the procedures and conditions for testing AI systems within realistic settings, requiring approval from the market surveillance authority.

Non-Personal Data
Non-personal data is information that does not relate to an identifiable individual and is not classified as personal data under the GDPR.

Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines that are programmed to think and learn like humans, often subject to regulatory frameworks.

Regulatory Supervision
Regulatory supervision involves the oversight by authorities to ensure compliance with laws and regulations, particularly in new technological domains like AI.

AI literacy
AI literacy encompasses the skills, knowledge, and understanding necessary for people to effectively deploy AI systems and recognize their opportunities and risks.

Real-world Testing
Real-world testing refers to the temporary evaluation of AI systems in actual conditions to gather data and ensure compliance with regulations.

Deep Fake
Deep fake technology involves AI-generated content that closely resembles real persons or objects, raising concerns about authenticity and potential harm.

Widespread Infringement
Widespread infringement refers to actions that violate laws protecting individual interests, potentially affecting multiple Member States.

Sandbox Plan
A sandbox plan allows for controlled testing of AI systems under regulatory supervision, limiting their operation time to ensure compliance.

Article 57
Article 57 outlines specific conditions that must be met for the testing of AI systems outside of laboratory settings.

EU Law
EU law encompasses legal frameworks that protect individual rights, including rules against actions causing harm across member states.

Collective Interests
Collective interests refer to the shared rights and welfare of individuals residing in multiple member states affected by AI systems and their deployment.

high-impact capabilities
High-impact capabilities refer to advanced abilities in AI that significantly affect markets or societies, particularly regarding public health and safety.<SEP>High-impact capabilities refer to the advanced abilities of AI models that match or exceed those of leading general-purpose AI models.

testing
Testing refers to the process of evaluating systems or subjects in real-world conditions to inform decisions, particularly regarding participation.

subject
Subject encompasses individuals or entities that are evaluated during testing to ensure that they are fully informed about the relevant aspects of testing.

deep fake
Deep fake refers to AI-generated or manipulated content, including images, audio, or video, that misleadingly resembles real persons or entities.

widespread infringement
Widespread infringement indicates actions contrary to Union law that could undermine the collective interests of individuals across multiple Member States.

systemic risk definition
Systemic risk in this context refers to risks that manifest due to the capabilities of AI systems, significantly impacting the union market and public welfare.

self-supervision
Self-supervision refers to a method in AI training where a model learns to label data without explicit supervision, enhancing its ability to perform diverse tasks.

floating-point operation
Floating-point operation is a mathematical process involving floating-point numbers, which are real numbers represented on computers in a specific format.

downstream provider
A downstream provider is an entity that offers an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, which integrates an AI model for various applications.

Floating-Point Operation
A floating-point operation is a mathematical action involving numbers that are represented in a specific format on computers, essential for calculations in AI models.

Mathematical Operation
Mathematical operations refer to processes or procedures involving numbers and variables that form the basis of computational tasks in AI systems.

Floating-Point Numbers

Algorithmic Systems
Algorithmic systems are the computational frameworks used in AI that can influence systemic risks in various applications.

Public Entities

The European AI Office is responsible for overseeing AI regulations, including development of compliance templates and guidelines.<SEP>The European Artificial Intelligence Office is responsible for overseeing the deployment of AI technologies, facilitating compliance, and reducing administrative burdens.<SEP>The European Artificial Intelligence Office is established as a regulatory body to oversee and facilitate artificial intelligence initiatives across Europe.<SEP>The European Artificial Intelligence Office was established by Commission Decision to develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI and contribute to the implementation of Union law on AI.

CENELEC

Annex VII
Annex VII details conformity assessment procedures involving notified bodies for high-risk AI systems.<SEP>Annex VII outlines the conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems and the involvement of notified bodies.<SEP>Annex VII outlines the conformity assessment procedures that high-risk AI systems must undergo, particularly following modifications.<SEP>Annex VII refers to a section of regulatory text concerning certificates issued by notified bodies for AI systems, focusing on the language requirements for validity.<SEP>Annex VII specifies requirements and guidelines for the amendment of related articles affecting AI systems.

Body Shape

Voice

Prosody
